subject: Exploratory Full-information Item Factor Analysis using theta where given randef() of mixedmirt()

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Exploratory Full-information Item Factor Analysis using theta where given randef() of mixedmirt()
parts:
Dear Phil,

I want to get factor structure coefficient of Exploratory Full-information Item Factor Analysis with multilevel modeling -- not IRT coefficients -- using theta where given randef() where generated mixedmirt() function with random group and random item slope model with mirt().

But as you already know, That's not available in mirt() or mixedmirt() function directly. So I imagine another way to do that.
I do not know in the depth about item response theory; I'm not a psychometrican, so I want to know that can make sense.


# estimating random theta (within)

fa_covdata <- data.frame(mydata)
i <- 1
itemtype <- 'gpcm'

      covdat <- data.frame(group = group)
      
      ranmod <- mixedmirt(fa_covdata, covdat, model=i, random = list(~ 1|group, ~ 1|items), itemtype = itemtype)
      summary(ranmod)
      raneff <- randef(ranmod)
      randTheta <- raneff$Theta
      
      
      result <- mirt(fa_covdata, i, itemtype=itemtype, rotate = 'geominQ', technical=list(NCYCLES=999999, MAXQUAD=9999999999999, customTheta = randTheta))
      

Always giving thanks. Cheers.

Seongho Bae

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Exploratory Full-information Item Factor Analysis using theta where given randef() of mixedmirt()
parts:
Hi Seongho,

Sorry, I don't think this will work. The customTheta input is generally used to define a grid of integration values, so defining it this way just makes the number of integration points much larger than the default (essentially, each response pattern is evaluated at each of these Theta values, then averaged over to obtain the expected value of the given response pattern). Hope that helps.

Phil
